subject: Bridge inventory commitment & multi-vendor signal for Acme deal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge inventory commitment & multi-vendor signal for Acme deal

Luis / team —

Following our call this morning, I wanted to capture the minimal mutual-action plan so procurement and ops can align across OEM vs cloud lanes. High level asks:

- Confirm OEM SKU lead times and whether there are any guaranteed ship windows we can rely on for the first tranche (we discussed 12-14 weeks, need explicit PO-to-ship SLAs).
- Provide firm per-SKU allocation lanes (microlanes) so we can map to our staging pools.
- Share any blackout dates or batch constraints in the OEM manufacturing queue.
- GCloud: can you confirm whether you can hold a short-term capacity backstop for 8 weeks post-delivery if we need transit buffering?

We need answers to the above by EOD Monday so we can produce a staggered PO ladder for the ACME committed capacity and the fallback pool. I attached the OEM quote we received yesterday — please flag any discrepancies.

Attachments: acme_oem_quote_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Manager, Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference

From: HPE Sales <hw-sales@hpe-oem.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acmeai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 14:40:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge inventory commitment & multi-vendor signal for Acme deal

Diego / Luis —

Quick response from our side:

- Confirmed lead time: standard lead time for the requested 80A SKUs is 11-13 weeks from PO receipt (we can commit to a 13-week cap for the first tranche with a signed PO).
- Allocation lanes: we can reserve a "priority lane" for ACME across two production runs (run A / run B). We will provide a per-serial allocation table by Monday.
- Blackouts: factory maintenance scheduled weeks 26-27 (mid-July) — small risk to late June POs.
- Shipping: FOB to Redwood staging; estimated transit 7-10 business days once shipped.

I've attached our updated quote and the provisional allocation template. If you need a binding SLA we can attach an expedited surcharge for guaranteed 11-week delivery.

Attachments: acme_oem_quote_v2.pdf (updated), hpe_allocation_template.xlsx

Regards,
Carlos Medina
Enterprise Sales — HPE OEM
hw-sales@hpe-oem.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Jun 2027 10:22:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge inventory commitment & multi-vendor signal for Acme deal

Diego —

Thanks for looping everyone. A couple tactical moves from procurement/infra perspective:

1) Staggered PO ladder: let's break down the committed 600-unit tranche into 3 POs (200 / 200 / 200) spaced 4 weeks apart. The first PO goes out immediately with the 13-week cap; second PO conditional based on run A/B allocation confirmation. That gives us a 4-week cadence to absorb any vendor slip.

2) Transit-buffering: request HPE to mark the first 50 units as "early release" so we can stage them onto our hot-pool for QA and smoke tests. That mitigates a 1-2 week transit variance.

3) Cloud backstop: Vanessa, can GCloud hold an emergency 2-week burst of equivalent capacity for June-July? We'll treat that as a paid backfill and only use if OEM slips.

4) Financials: Naomi, need a quick estimate of surcharge impact if we take HPE's 11-week guaranteed lane vs the standard 13-week. Also flag customs/port hold risks for FOB shipping.

Quoted below is the HPE line on blackouts — factory maintenance in weeks 26-27. We'll avoid sending a PO that lands in that window.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acmeai.com>, hw-sales@hpe-oem.com, partner@gcloud.example.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final mutual action plan: PO ladder, backstop, and next steps (ACME)

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. Below is the consolidated mutual-action plan we will act on this week. Please treat as the working runbook until we have signed PO/DocuSign.

1) PO ladder and timing
   - PO-1: 200 units, issue Tue 15 Jun 2027 (HPE 13-week cap). Target ship window: week of 12 Sep 2027.
   - PO-2: 200 units, tentative issue Tue 13 Jul 2027 (conditional on allocation table).
   - PO-3: 200 units, tentatively Aug 10 2027.

2) Transit-buffering and early release
   - HPE to mark 50 units from PO-1 as early release for staging. Redwood to confirm receipt plan.

3) Cloud backstop
   - GCloud Solutions to hold a 2-week emergency burst equivalent to 80 units for July 2027 (paid allocation). Partner confirmed availability; please see attached gcloud_capacity_response.msg for their formal reply.

4) Manufacturing blackouts
   - Avoid PO timing that would fall into HPE factory maintenance (weeks 26-27).

5) Financial / SLA options
   - Naomi to circulate surcharge delta for guaranteed 11-week lane vs standard 13-week. Decision by Jun 10.

6) Next steps & owners
   - Diego: issue PO-1 draft and open DocuSign (target Jun 10).
   - Karthik: finalize staging and transit buffer plan.
   - Marissa: coordinate with Sales Ops for invoice cadence and HubSpot deal update (HS-ACME-42).
   - HPE / GCloud: provide per-serial allocation file and DocuSign-ready commercial terms by Jun 10.

Attachments: fleet_commit_matrix.xlsx, acme_oem_quote_v2.pdf, gcloud_capacity_response.msg

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Manager, Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0198
